solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sticky stuff covering lettuce is sugar

indicators.note: the glue is wrapped around the lettuce, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: glue is the classic sticky stuff
cos is a variety of lettuce, the romaine

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the gooey dressing coating their salad is just sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar found in fruit and blood.

clue.text: Retire, worried by look from this layabout

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: worried here means tugged about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who wants to retire is anxious about a look from an idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A loiterer hangs about idly, which is what a layabout does.

clue.text: Christian who's new to chalice (not European)

indicators.note: the letters are made new by being rearranged
the letter for European is taken out of chalice

explanation.surface: A believer who has only just come to using the chalice, not being European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops E from CHALICE, leaving CHALIC; 'new' rearranges TO plus CHALIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic is a member of the Roman Catholic Church, a Christian denomination.

clue.text: Corporate excesses?

parts.note: corporate is read as to do with the body (corpus), so the excesses are flab round the waist

explanation.definitionFit: Spare tyres is slang for rolls of fat around the middle, bodily excess.

clue.text: Atmosphere in university welcomed by a Royal Academician

indicators.note: being welcomed means being taken in, so the university letter goes inside

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: The mood in a university as it welcomes a Royal Academician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed by' puts U between A and RA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or air surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: Everybody on board tug is fat

indicators.note: on board means inside, so the word for everybody goes within

parts.note: to tow is to tug or pull along
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone on the tugboat is overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is hard animal fat used for candles and soap.

clue.text: Women crews use these for training

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Female rowing crews do workouts with gym equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Weights are the dumbbells and barbells used in strength training.

clue.text: Standing, look around trade union

indicators.note: the look surrounds the union abbreviation

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly

explanation.surface: Someone standing about looks around the trade union office.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means standing or reputation, as in a figure of great stature.

clue.text: Shoot a scene, initially in favourite city

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant

indicators.note: the initial letter goes inside the word for favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: only the opening letter of scene is wanted

explanation.surface: A film director wants to shoot a scene first in their favourite city.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary.

clue.text: Wind and fog really throws regulars

parts.note: mist is a light fog

indicators.note: the word really gives up its odd letters in a regular pattern

explanation.surface: A forecaster grumbles that wind and fog really throw off the regular plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throws regulars' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'really', R, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong cold wind blowing down the Rhône valley in southern France.

clue.text: Good area with weak source of illumination

parts.note: slight means frail or weak

explanation.surface: A good area to sit, but with only a weak lamp to see by.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp burning coal gas was the main source of street and home lighting in Victorian times.

clue.text: Welcome must include note — the Spanish land outside city

indicators.note: the word for welcome takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
NB, nota bene, is a note to mark something well
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A welcome sign must include a note in Spanish about land outside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A green belt is protected countryside surrounding a city where building is restricted.

clue.text: Unlikely way of learning about return of the setter

indicators.note: the rote learning wraps around the turned-round word

parts.note: learning by rote is memorising through repetition

indicators.note: the word for the setter is turned to read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A teacher thinks it unlikely that rote learning will bring the setter back.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of a crossword conventionally refers to themself as ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote chance is an unlikely one, a distant possibility.

clue.text: Make no progress in the main

definitions.meaning: to stay in the same place, getting nowhere
the main is the sea, where a swimmer stays afloat upright by kicking

explanation.definitionFit: Treading water means staying afloat without moving forward, hence figuratively making no progress.

clue.text: Limit availability after design style award

indicators.note: the limiting word comes after the design style

parts.note: deco, as in Art Deco, is a 1920s and 30s design style
to ration is to limit the supply of something

explanation.surface: Supply is restricted after a design award.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is a medal or honour, an award.

clue.text: Knee pain? Oddly, it's the cap!

indicators.note: the odd-positioned letters of the two words are kept

explanation.surface: A soldier with an aching knee blames the cap of their uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes letters 1, 3, 5, 7 of KNEEPAIN: K, E, P, I.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat circular top and a peak.

clue.text: Lease must be vacated after long-standing account

indicators.note: the emptied word comes after the word for long-standing

parts.note: chronic means persisting for a long time

indicators.note: the word lease is emptied of its inner letters, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A tenant must leave the property after a long-running dispute over the account.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written historical account of events in order.

clue.text: E=mc2, say — quite a different case of omission

indicators.note: the letters are made different by being reordered
the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: Einstein's famous formula, which is quite another matter as a case of something left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges QUITEA into EQUATI; 'case of' takes the outer letters of 'omission', O and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein's E=mc2 is the best-known example of a mathematical statement that two expressions are equal.

clue.text: Foundation students covering graduate game

parts.note: a base is a foundation
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
L is a learner, so two are students

explanation.surface: Foundation-year students and a graduate play a game together.
explanation.walkthrough: L, the learner driver's plate, stands for a learner, so a pair of them can be students.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is the American bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: European husband's embrace

parts.note: a husband is a spouse

explanation.surface: A man from Europe holding someone in his arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to embrace or adopt it.

clue.text: Company gets fined for breaking trust

indicators.note: the word fined is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm that is fined for breach of trust.
explanation.definitionFit: To confide is to trust someone with a secret, or to place trust in them.

clue.text: One in four gets a bike of sorts

definitions.meaning: a quadruplet, one of four children born together

explanation.definitionFit: Quad is short for quadruplet and also for a quad bike.

clue.text: Gear that makes son utter obscenities about Liverpool, say

indicators.note: son and swear go around the example of a port city

parts.note: to swear is to curse
Liverpool is a port city, an example of a port

explanation.surface: A football kit that makes a boy curse about Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool is a major English seaport, so it stands for any port.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportswear is clothing, or kit, worn for sport.

clue.text: Straight out without a good top!

indicators.note: the letters of straight are put out of order

parts.note: a is itself, and G is the abbreviation for good; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone goes straight out without a decent top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges STRAIGHT once 'without' has removed A and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is a simple short-sleeved top.

clue.text: Astonished — a day to go round part of Hampton Court

indicators.note: a and the day abbreviation wrap around the garden feature

parts.note: Hampton Court Palace, near London, has a famous hedge maze in its gardens

explanation.surface: A visitor plans a day trip to walk round part of Hampton Court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' puts MAZE between A and D. Hampton Court is a Tudor palace by the Thames with a famous hedge maze.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed is a direct synonym of astonished, both meaning greatly surprised.

clue.text: Not available to film new branch

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu
to shoot is to film

explanation.surface: A director is unavailable to film at the company's new branch.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side shoot from a plant, or a new organisation grown from a parent one.

clue.text: State occasion's beginning with lots unfinished

indicators.note: only the first letter of occasion is taken
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: many means lots

explanation.surface: A state occasion begins with many guests not done.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sultanate, a state on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Understand one story mostly showing numerical information

parts.note: dig is slang for understand or appreciate
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Grasp one story that mostly displays numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital displays and data present information as digits, numbers rather than dials.

clue.text: Pretentious air true of the stars?

parts.note: side is an old British word for swagger or putting on airs
real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: A grand manner that is genuine belongs only to the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE, a pompous or conceited manner, is chiefly British usage ('to put on side').
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means relating to the stars, as in sidereal time measured against them.

clue.text: Any line crossed in a daft way

indicators.note: crossed lines are tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Any line drawn across the page was done foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, so the adverb means foolishly.
